nodes.summary: The encodings of words over `T`: the words over `T ⊕ Unit` consisting of left letters followed by a single end marker.
nodes.title: Language of end-marker encoded words

nodes.summary: After the end marker, the encoding DFA can only be in its accepting state on empty input.
nodes.title: Encoding DFA after the end marker accepts only the empty input

nodes.summary: The dead state of the encoding DFA stays dead.
nodes.title: Dead state of the encoding DFA is absorbing

nodes.summary: The encoding DFA accepts exactly the encodings: it reaches the accepting state on an encoding.
nodes.title: Encoding DFA accepts every end-marker encoding

nodes.summary: The encoding DFA stays in its start state while reading left letters.
nodes.title: Encoding DFA stays in its start state on left letters

nodes.summary: The DFA for the encodings: state `inl false` while reading left letters, `inl true` after the end marker (the accepting state), and `inr ()` dead once anything follows the end marker.
nodes.title: DFA recognizing end-marker encodings

nodes.summary: Encode a word by copying it to the left summand and appending the end marker `Sum.inr ()`.
nodes.title: End-marker encoding of a word

nodes.summary: Erasing an encoding recovers the word.
nodes.title: Erasing the end-marker encoding recovers the word

nodes.summary: Erase the end marker: a left letter maps to its one-letter word, the end marker maps to the empty word.
nodes.title: End-marker erasure

nodes.summary: The encoding DFA reaches the accepting state only on encodings.
nodes.title: Encoding DFA accepts only end-marker encodings

nodes.summary: Every deterministic context-free language is context-free: the encoded language is accepted by a pushdown automaton, hence context-free; intersecting with the regular language of encodings and erasing the end marker recovers the original language.
nodes.title: Deterministic context-free languages are context-free

nodes.summary: A language is deterministic context-free when some deterministic pushdown automaton with finite state and stack alphabets, whose transitions consume letters from a finite set, accepts by empty stack exactly the end-marker encodings of its words.
nodes.title: Deterministic context-free language

nodes.summary: A pushdown automaton is deterministic when every transition set has at most one element, and an available `ε`-transition precludes every consuming transition from the same state and stack symbol.
nodes.title: Deterministic pushdown automaton

nodes.summary: The encodings of words form a regular language.
nodes.title: End-marker encodings form a regular language

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
